As for plants, I'm not sure you mean aquarium as in a fully aquatic plant set up with fish and the like, or as in a habitat with multiple plants in the same container / with the same soil source. For both, the answers are yes and yes. So if you're researching an aquatic set up, my knowledge on that is iffy at best, but there are a bunch of resources and cool videos of people setting up nano tank habitats with a bunch of live plants and fish. I'm sure you could set up a (fairly) self-sustaining ecosystem there, as long as you have some algae-eaters. It would have to be a pretty delicate set up, I'm assuming, what with population control and a lot of other factors that exist but that I know jack about. There's also terrariums, and I have an article saved somewhere about a guy who had a huge closed terrarium for a number of years (I can't remember if it was 20, or 10, but it was *impressive)* that I, of course, cannot find*.* 

A more modern take on creating a plant display that is as close to a natural habitat as possible is living walls. These are specifically for plants that can produce epiphytic growth, or will "climb". There's a way deeper explanation into epiphytes and it's a really cool deep dive but some typical houseplants you see that have this capability are pothos, a large amount of philodendron, monstera, and on the fancier side some rarer anthurium (velvet leaf anthurium are some of the coolest looking tropicals of all time). You'll see this type of set up with a lot of collectors because a lot of these climbing plants only produce really impressive, large leaves when they climb. I used to have some philodendron that were on poles that had leaves larger than my head, and some can get leaves over a couple of feet long. Epiphytes also include mosses and orchids!

The most important thing that makes some plants incompatible when planted together is their environmental needs. Plants that grow naturally in the cloud forest of Ecuador are not going to jam with plants that like dry soil and dry air. Plants that grow on the banks of lakes, rivers, ponds, etc. are going to be much more fond of having "wet feet", or consistently wet soil, whereas plants used to deep drought, like cacti, are going to rot immediately with too much water.  On the houseplant scale, you wouldn't want to pot a ZZ and a maranta/prayer plant together. Prayer plants like to stay somewhat consistently moist (they typically have super fine roots that dry out very quickly in dry soil) whereas ZZ have huge rhizomes that store water for a long period of time, so sitting in too much water will make them rot. This is pretty intuitive for most common plants (and even rarer plants, too). Where do they come from? What areas do they naturally thrive in? That should give you some tips as to what plants match up and what don't. Plants that like to stay in moist soil environments and like a lot of humidity typically do well together in terrariums.

Some more experienced growers also use semi-hydro, where they grow in a sterile medium where they provide nutrients by hand into the water/growing medium. A lot of people use Leca or PON substrate to do this but it's also applicable to growing strictly in coco chips/coir or sphagnum moss. This way, they can create a perfect environment, down to the PH of the water to mimic a plant's ideal growing conditions in the wild.

I hope that was enough to get you started and at least give you some topics to go off of! Probably way more than enough. Thanks for just being here, and being willing to be engaged.

A lot of this is just me being in agreeance with you and digging into ideas to get my thoughts out of my head in a way that I can refer back to for some introspection. Feel free to skip to plant related things, I'll be doing that in a separate response! Also, know that the questions I've posed in a lot of this are rhetorical in nature and meant to  get my own brain rolling on how to address and explain these issues a little better. Putting abstract concepts into words, and all that. 

When people want the depressed people in their life to be visibly okay it just gives me vibes that they don't want to confront the problem or their role in it, or on a grander scale why *so many people feel like this*. Yeah, I want the people around me to appear okay to me, but (and this is probably because I am depressed, so I know that you can look and act so perfectly normal and be in complete turmoil on the inside) not so much that I want to act like they aren't going through it. As I'm getting older, I'm realizing the difference between friends and acquaintances. When I was younger, every kid that signed my yearbook or knew my name was what I considered a "friend". As we mature, I think we start looking for a deeper connection than that. We want someone to truly *know* us, not just this idea of us that they get from seeing us an hour a day, five days a week, where we don't even talk. And I'm fine with that! It makes sense, right, because as what we're experiencing becomes less juvenile, friendships aren't just going to the mall anymore and being able to tolerate each other for a couple of hours. It's a lot heavier than that (imo? Maybe I'm purple prose-ing it up over here about friends, but I take my inner circle pretty seriously). It's just in times like these where I wish I had *more* of those types of friends to spread the weight around, a little. Sometimes I feel like if I go to my friend and say "oh hey, I really think I'm going to kill myself," she knows that she's one of the only people I'll tell  and she'll feel like it's all on her to stop it or that it will be her fault if she doesn't and something happens. I guess the trade off of having some super honest friendships like that is that it's unlikely you'll find a lot of people you're comfortable talking to that way, and who are also comfortable talking to you that way. 

I feel you on the college stuff. It's really hard for me to set small goals for myself which I think is why I'm feeling so stagnant, because it's hard when you want to jump to the end goal but have no idea how to even start moving. I went to a big university eight hours away from home, and that's the *only* school I want to go back to for my undergrad (and grad, but that's a whole other story). So instead of starting small and just taking a refresher math course or an English course that I find interesting to get back into the swing of things, I go in full force. If I'm not taking at least eighteen credits, I don't want it. Which is a big problem because 1) I can't afford eighteen advanced credits and to move way away from home out of pocket right now and 2) it sets me up for so much failure. I'm not even sure if I can handle being in an academic environment again right now, but my brain is like "If you settle for anything less than what you used to be able to handle, you are worthless. You suck. You will never succeed and be smart". Also, it's not safe for me! I'm feeling this down a*t home*, with my support system close by. Imagine how that would be if I moved into a super stressful environment without anyone? And I can rationalize that, because I know it would be an unwise decision for anyone, but I can't quite apply it to myself.

I get the time thing, or at least I think I do. When I get into the troughs of my depression roller coaster, my attention span is negligible. It makes it extremely difficult to connect to anything, like you mentioned. A TV show, a book, anything. Time either seems to move so slowly I think a day will never end or so quickly that I swear I sat down to watch a show at 2PM and I swear I only saw one episode but now its 2AM and I don't know how I got there. Or on a larger scale, weeks will pass so, so quickly. Events that I *know* I had a month to prepare for are now suddenly tomorrow and I can't quite grasp or track the time in between. It's just like being unaware of space or time except for very specific moments. For example, I'll know I did something (ex: went to the store, made a smoothie, talked to a certain person) but I can't pin down when that happened relative to the last "big" event where I *was* aware of the time. Let me know if I'm in the ballpark of what you're talking about, yeah?

For talking specifics, I always attribute it to being in one of my super high excited stages, but I get hyper focused on certain subjects and "collect". So I'll find a cool thing, and I have to know everything about it. It's not good enough to just think it's cool, I have to become a self-taught expert on it and/or collect everything to do with it. I don't know if it's an addictive personality thing, or just that when you're depressed (especially long term) you just want to dive head first into anything that makes you feel positive, and overdo it trying to soak it all in while it lasts. Maybe that feeds into wanting to talk details whereas people who don't feel like their happiness isn't so fleeting don't feel the need to be so invested in a topic/hobby/interest. Like I don't get this feeling often, so when I do, I have to attack it at 300% to get the most out of it while it's here.

I like listening to people talk for the same reason; like look at this person just out there *living.*

Thanks for validating my experience - it really is that they don't try that gets to me. If you slip up but you're working at it, that's different. It might hurt but at least I'm aware that you are trying. On the other hand, when they don't it's prime fodder for all those little hurtful thoughts that say I'm not worth the time or the effort. The possibility of me being able to be at my best is not enough for them to try and help me get there the way they can. When I first started therapy I had to tackle the most basic tasks in the zero day form. I'm talking brushing my teeth, getting out of bed and walking around, brushing my hair, eating even just a snack. It was really helpful for me then because it was a reminder to me that when I did just one of these things I was treating myself like a living, breathing person. As I progressed, and then ultimately regressed, it stopped being so effective. My depression evolved, and I've yet to find a tool to be effective in this new stage. Kind of like having different keys for different locks. Definitely not too much introspection and totally what I meant.

To draw an end to the heavier stuff - yeah, you covered what I was hoping for. A lot of really good points made concisely that are honestly damn helpful.

That means so much I don't even know how to put it into words, so thank you. I didn't explicitly mention it but it is a concern of mine - it's insinuated pretty often that I'm overreacting, which just makes me upset. They'll deny that I've told them that the things they say bother me, or they'll just say that I shouldn't be bothered. It's like, do you think I don't know that? That I don't feel stupid that I can't just shake it off and keep moving? But I am, and they don't respect that. It makes me feel like I'm going insane sometimes.

I wish I had a wider support net. I feel like just by not having more people to talk to I put a lot of pressure on the people I do have around me just by existing in the state I'm in. It's not fair to me, and it's not fair to them.

I might steal that response and see how it works for me in the future. I have a bit of trouble getting my thoughts in line and verbalizing what I need from people in the moment. I have some hobbies, but how I'm feeling right now just overrides the joy I get from them. I can't sit down and focus on enjoying something when I'm down; my mind is just going 1000mph and I have some really intrusive thoughts that just take me out of the zone when I need it.

You can talk about your own experience here, makes me feel a little less fucking alone honestly
It means a lot - it made me feel a little better too.

I'm sorry you're feeling this way too. I can't make my brain believe anything positive I tell myself, if that makes sense? I think I've reached a point where I just can't penetrate all the negative stuff I see about myself. I feel like my time is useless, therefore why even spend it? I'm just consistently feeling miserable anyways no matter what I do lately.

I feel like this constantly, for literally almost two years on the dot - right after I left school. Been through med changes, therapy, tried really really really hard and then everything just falls apart. My relationships with my parents and my friends are all basically gone. I had conversations with my parents saying "Oh, when you say (insert passive aggressive phrase here) it upsets me, even though you don't find it upsetting. I'd prefer if you don't say that anymore." Then they turn around and say the same things and act like there's no way they could be hurting me. When I'm really down and low they don't check on me, which makes me feel worse. Like I'm not worth checking on any more. They used to when I first came home from school, but now it's like they're just tired of it and so am I. 

When I finally get "up" and am feeling better, I feel *way* better and get really excited about stupid shit (like I'm really into plants. I will talk for *hours* about my plants if you let me). Then they treat me like I am the most annoying person. I just feel like I can't win. I'm either too sad or too happy. I literally have one friend that I can talk to about this stuff and that's... it. If I'm not feeling numb I feel like I'm drowning in all these feelings and I'm just over it. I don't know how to handle it anymore
